02/13.10.2017 Learned counsel for the petitioner is directed to implead the State of Jharkhand, through the Principal Secretary, Department of Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare, Government of Jharkhand, Ranchi as the respondent No.3 in the present writ petition.

entities.text: Department of Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare, Government of Jharkhand, Ranchi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Let necessary insertion in the cause title of the writ petition be made in course of the day.
Learned J.C to A.G accepts notice on behalf of the newly impleaded respondent No.3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner undertakes to serve two copies of the writ petition upon the learned counsel for the State.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that a notice contained in Letter No. 2030 dated 22.08.2017 was issued by the Ranchi Municipal Corporation asking a show cause as to why the license of the petitioner's trade premises be not cancelled for his alleged involvement in making trade of adulterated oil as well as for the reason that the license of the said premises was given in the name of one Manoj Kumar Agarwal, but the Income Tax Return of the said business premises shows that the same has been filed in the name of Manoj Chhaparia.

The petitioner submitted his reply before the Ranchi Municipal Corporation vide letter dated 26.08.2017 stating, inter alia, that the sample of the edible oil taken by the State authorities from the trade premises of the petitioner was sent to the State Food Testing Laboratory, Namkum, Ranchi and

entities.text: State Food Testing Laboratory, Namkum, Ranchi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
as per its report dated 21.06.2017,
it was found that the said sample corforms to the prescribed standard for refined palmolein, but the same has been found to be a misbranded one under Section 3(zf)(C)(i) of the Food Safety and Manoj Kumar Agarwal Alias Manoj ... vs Ranchi Municipal Corporation

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Through ... on 13 October, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103454368/
1 Standard Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the said Act') for which a proceeding has been drawn by the Deputy Commissioner, Ranchi under Section 52 of the said Act.
It was further replied by the petitioner that Manoj Kumar Agarwal and Manoj Chhaparia are the same persons.
The petitioner also submitted several documents in support of the said fact.

The learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner has appeared in the said proceeding under Section 52 of the said Act and the reply would be filed soon before the Court of the Deputy Commissioner, Ranchi.
It is further submitted that unless the proceeding under Section 52 of the said Act is concluded, the petitioner cannot be pre-judged to be guilty of misbranding of the edible oil.

In the aforesaid circumstances, the impugned order dated 03.10.2017 whereby, the license of the trade premises of the petitioner has been cancelled by the Ranchi Municipal Corporation, Ranchi, is premature and arbitrary and, therefore, the operation of the said order may be stayed.
Mr. Prashant Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the Ranchi Municipal Corporation and learned J.C to A.G pray for and are allowed four weeks' time to file counter affidavit.
Put up this case on 12.12.2017 under the heading "For Admission".
Till then, the status-quo, as exists today, shall be maintained by the parties with respect to the trade premises of the petitioner in question.

Satish/- (RAJESH SHANKAR, J)
